report.summary: Chunk 1 of daedalus/eval/provenance.py defines ProvenanceCheck, PROBE_SOURCE, and check_import_provenance to verify that the candidate's interpreter resolves daedalus from the candidate tree. All docstring claims are kept. Observation: subprocess inherits environment, so PYTHONPATH could skew results.
risks: line 76 | high | check_import_provenance does not sanitize environment; PYTHONPATH could cause daedalus to resolve outside candidate tree even if probe passes | Confirm that caller clears PYTHONPATH before calling, or add env parameter to function

claims.text: The loop graded the host against itself
claims.why: This claim describes a historical bug in the runner, not code in this chunk.

claims.text: the runner now uses sys.executable -m pytest with cwd set to the worktree
claims.why: The runner implementation is not in this chunk.

claims.text: This module exists because that is a MECHANISM, not a VERIFICATION.
claims.why: The module performs a verification (check_import_provenance) rather than relying on the mechanism.

claims.text: a failed check voids the EVALUATION rather than scoring the candidate

claims.why: Performance claim not verifiable from source alone.

claims.text: Run in the CANDIDATE's interpreter, cwd and environment -- not here.
claims.why: check_import_provenance uses subprocess.run with cwd=base and executable from the candidate (or sys.executable).

claims.text: Reports rather than asserts, so the caller decides.
claims.why: Returns ProvenanceCheck, does not raise or exit.

claims.text: A probe that exited non-zero on mismatch would be indistinguishable from a probe that failed to start
claims.why: The function treats non-zero returncode as failure, same as probe not starting.

claims.text: Whether an evaluation in ``root`` would score the code in ``root``.
claims.why: The ok field indicates this, and check_import_provenance checks if daedalus resolves under root.
as_error returns string containing 'EVALUATION VOID' and 'not a candidate failure'.

claims.text: A probe that will not start, times out, returns unparseable output, or cannot import daedalus at all reports ok=False
claims.why: Each of those cases returns ProvenanceCheck(False, ...) in the code.

claims.text: __path__ is checked too: a namespace package has no __file__
claims.why: candidates includes both daedalus_file and daedalus_path items.

claims.text: a candidate whose package dir lost its __init__.py would otherwise resolve to None and be read as "no answer" rather than "wrong tree".
claims.why: By checking candidates list, if __file__ is None but __path__ points inside root, it's still caught.

observations.what: check_import_provenance does not validate that the subprocess executable exists or is the same as the candidate's interpreter; it uses sys.executable as fallback.
The probe source captures sys.argv[0] and sys.path[0] but these are never used in the verification logic.
The function does not set an environment for the subprocess; it inherits the current environment, which may include PYTHONPATH.
